motion.name: duration-xs
motion.purpose: Press and hover; the web pressed overlay goes out in 100ms on easing-exit.

motion.name: duration-sm
motion.purpose: Fades, popover enter, presence fade/lift, row enter, check-off row fade, reduced-motion fade.

motion.name: duration-md
motion.purpose: Dialog, toast, presence rise/scale/slide, the rows closing up.

motion.name: exit-durations
motion.purpose: Exits of xs / sm / md / lg: popover 110, dialog and toast 160, sheet and the revealed route 200.

motion.name: easing-enter
motion.purpose: Things appearing; also the web route animations.

motion.name: easing-exit
motion.purpose: Things leaving; the check-off row fade.

motion.name: easing-move
motion.purpose: In-place change: the rows closing up, layout shifts.

motion.name: spring-sheet
motion.purpose: Sheet drag release; a drag past 30% of its height or a flick >= 800 dp/s dismisses.

motion.name: reduced
motion.purpose: Replaces travel and scale everywhere; never nothing (the kit sets ReduceMotion.Never and picks the fade itself).

motion.name: check-off
motion.value: circle fills on press-in · content fades 1→0 160ms easing-exit · box closes up 220ms easing-move · onDone from completion
motion.purpose: Owner Q2: a plain fade, no dissolve; reduced motion fades 160 then closes at once.

motion.name: presence-presets
motion.value: fade · lift 4px up · rise 8px up · drop 4px · scale 0.96 · slide 16px from trailing; fade/lift 160/110, the rest 220/160
motion.purpose: Presence enter/exit; the toast rises 8px in and drops 4px out.

motion.name: overlays
motion.value: sheet 280/200 own-height travel + scrim fade · dialog 0.96→1 220 / →0.98 160 · popover 0.98→1 160/110 from the anchor edge
motion.purpose: Each overlay leaves the way it came.

motion.name: route-web
motion.value: push: translateX 12px + fade 280ms easing-enter · revealed screen: -12px + fade 200ms · reduced: fade 160ms
motion.purpose: CSS keyframes on [data-pace-route]; tab switches have none.

motion.name: skeleton-breath
motion.value: opacity 1 ↔ 0.7, 600ms each way (1.2s period), after a 300ms delay
motion.purpose: Loading placeholders; still under reduced motion.

narrative.overview:
Pace is a school notebook used as a tool: cool squared paper, ballpoint-blue ink and a red margin rule. The ink does every interactive job (the one primary action, links, the switch that is on, the chosen chip, the selection bar, the focus ring, done); the red margin is status only (the now-line on Day, the expected-length mark on the running line, overdue, Urgent, destructive, the waiting count). Everything at rest is neutral paper and graphite text, so the content (task titles, times, the day's shape) is the brightest thing on the screen.

The app works in Operate mode on every surface: the person is in the middle of a task, so scanability, consistency and platform expectations outrank expression. The world contributes type rhythm, palette, density and one signature detail; the shell, navigation and controls are the platform's (a Material navigation bar and ripple on Android, web semantics and a CSS state layer on the web). A screen is one ground with grouped list sections on it; elevation is only for things that float. Time is drawn as time: one formatter, tabular figures, and on Day a rail whose bars line up with the rows they belong to.

The signature lives on Day and in the running card: Day's rail sits on a faint dot grid (only inside the rail), crossed by a red now-line; the running activity reads as a 2 px ink line with a 1 px red mark at its expected length. Colour is never a dot: a project, category or running activity leads with a 32 hue tile (its tint, an icon in its ink). Both themes, both scripts (Latin and Cyrillic) and the worst case (long Russian names, 1 284 tasks, font scale 1.6) are part of the design, not tests after it. With no stored preference and no light OS setting, the page starts dark.
keyCharacteristics: One cool accent (ink blue) for every interactive job; red is status, never decoration.
One surface with grouped lists; separators only between rows of a group, inset to the text.
Inter only, thirteen fixed type roles with a phone and a desktop column, tabular figures for every number.
A 4-pt spacing scale and seven radii; the Tailwind scales are replaced, so nothing off-scale exists.
Depth by tonal step; the overlay shadow only on floating layers, an inner hairline in dark.
Every press answers within a frame; every overlay leaves the way it came; nothing exceeds 300 ms, and reduced motion is a 160 ms fade, never nothing.

rules.name: The One Ink Rule
rules.body: Ink blue is the only interactive colour, and a screen at rest shows at most one filled ink element. On desktop the sidebar's New task button is that element, so screens keep their own actions tonal until something is ready to commit.

rules.name: The Red Margin Rule
rules.body: Red marks status: the now-line, the expected-length mark, overdue, Urgent, destructive, errors, what waits. It is never decoration, never a brand flourish, never a category.

rules.name: The Pen Colour Rule
rules.body: A coloured thing is its hue's tint under its ink: a project tag, a coloured chip at rest, a hue tile leading a project, category or running activity row, a bar on Day's rail (with a stroke edge, because the tint alone is under 3:1). Colour is never shown as a dot. Importance has no colour of its own: Urgent is a red word, Low (Необязательно) draws the title in `label-secondary` at 400, Normal shows nothing.

rules.name: The Logo Lime Rule
rules.body: Lime belongs to the Pace mark, favicon and app icon. It never appears as an interface colour.

rules.name: The No Kicker Rule
rules.body: Nothing sits above a title: no eyebrow, no kicker, no small-caps date. The date is a subtitle under the large title (Now, Day) or lives in the period control (Week, History, Insights).

rules.name: The Tabular Time Rule
rules.body: Every duration, clock and count uses a numeric role or the `numeric` flag (tabular figures) and one core formatter: Russian gets a non-breaking space before units («2 ч 05 мин», «1 284»), a decimal comma, and hours roll into days past 48 h.

rules.name: The One Section Header Rule
rules.body: A section header is `subhead`, sentence case, `label-secondary`, 24 px above and 8 px below, inset to line up with cell text, announced as a heading of its level, with at most one trailing count or action.

rules.name: The One Surface Rule
rules.body: A screen is one ground with grouped lists on it. No cards in cards, no hairline around every container, no bordered boxes stacked in a column.

rules.name: The Notebook Grid Rule
rules.body: The dot grid (a 1 px dot every 12 px in `grid`) exists only inside Day's rail. It never becomes a page background, a card texture or a decoration elsewhere.

rules.name: The Float-Only Rule
rules.body: Elevation is for things that float (sheets, dialogs, popovers, toasts, banners). Lists, rows, groups, the running card and notices sit flat on their ground. Tooltips float on a hairline, without a shadow.

rules.name: The One Boundary Rule
rules.body: Content containers mark their edge by fill alone: no border around groups, cells, the running card, chips, tags or tiles. A line appears only where a fill cannot carry the boundary at 3:1: a control without a fill (`outline`), the switch track off, the segmented thumb (`label-tertiary` edge), the destructive button (2 px danger), a rail bar (its stroke), and the edge of a toast or tooltip floating over content.

rules.name: The Nested Radius Rule
rules.body: Inner radius = outer radius − padding, never below `xs`: a 16-radius group with 8 inset holds 8-radius controls.

rules.name: The Pill-or-Plate Rule
rules.body: Small labels and toggles are pills (chips, tags, badges, switches, segments, indicators); anything that holds a layout (buttons, fields, tiles, groups, cards, overlays) is a rounded rectangle from the scale.

dos: **Do** keep ink blue (#2E4AD6 / #97A9FF) as the only interactive colour, with at most one filled ink element per screen at rest.
**Do** reserve Red Margin (#C3352B / #FF8274) for the now-line, the expected-length mark, overdue, Urgent, destructive, errors and what waits.
**Do** draw a coloured thing as its hue's tint under its ink: a pill tag, a coloured chip at rest, a 32 hue tile leading its row.
**Do** put every number through a numeric role (tabular figures) and the core formatter, with non-breaking spaces in Russian.
**Do** build screens as one `bg-app` ground with `bg-cell` groups (`lg`, 16) and inset separators.

**Do** build every control on the kit's `Pressable` so it gets the one state layer: `fill-1` hover, `fill-3` ripple / `fill-2` overlay, a 2 px + 2 px ink focus ring, `label-quaternary` + `fill-1` when disabled.
**Do** add every new colour pair to `pairs.ts` and check every decision in both themes, in Russian, at 320 / 390 / 1440 and at font scale 1.6.
**Do** pair every overlay's enter with its exit, stay at or under 300 ms, chain the next step on completion, and give each a 160 ms reduced-motion fade.
donts: **Don't** put an eyebrow, kicker or small label above a title.
**Don't** use red as decoration, as a category colour or as a brand accent.
**Don't** use the logo lime (#5E8C00 / #C8F03C) anywhere but the logo, favicon and app icon.
**Don't** show "Normal" importance, or give importance its own colour beyond the red Urgent word.
**Don't** nest cards in cards, outline every container, or add a border where the fill already holds 3:1.
**Don't** put shadows on content; the overlay shadow belongs to sheets, dialogs, popovers, toasts and banners.
**Don't** use text glyphs (↵, ⋯) as icons, an outlined square for Stop, or a pulsing running dot.
**Don't** show colour as a dot; a coloured thing is a tint under its ink.
**Don't** spread the dot grid beyond Day's rail.
**Don't** use off-scale spacing, radii, font sizes or arbitrary values, a bare pressable, or a direct lucide import; lint rejects them.
**Don't** dim disabled controls with opacity, or show state by colour alone.
**Don't** animate list mounts, filter changes, tab switches or day switches, or pair a fixed timer with an animation.
